# Embedded WFM RDS dependencies

- redsea 1.3.1: windytan/redsea commit `7555c9f6259d50718697ee8c9f218ea012c6892c`, from `~/prj/ref/openwebrx/ext/redsea`. License: repository `redsea/LICENSE` (MIT); source-file ISC-style notices are retained. `src/io/input.hh` contains only the MPX buffer declaration instead of the file/CLI readers, and `ext/iconvpp/iconv.hpp` uses a built-in UCS-2/Latin-1 to UTF-8 adapter on Android, Windows and macOS (Bionic and the Windows CRT do not provide iconv; macOS would need an extra `-liconv`); desktop Linux keeps the glibc iconv path. No CLI, libsndfile, subprocess, or separate tuner is linked.
- liquid-dsp 1.6.0: https://github.com/jgaeddert/liquid-dsp/releases/tag/v1.6.0 (tag archive), license `liquid-dsp-1.6.0/LICENSE` (MIT). Native CMake compiles scalar library sources, including upstream 57 kHz recovery components used by redsea. The tag archive contains source and build scaffolding; generated `include/liquid/liquid.h` is a copy of its own `include/liquid.h` for upstream redsea's header path. `liquid-config.h.in` produces a portable scalar `config.h` in the CMake build tree on both Linux and Android; no source-tree configure run is required.
- nlohmann/json 3.11.3: https://github.com/nlohmann/json/releases/tag/v3.11.3, single include `nlohmann/json.hpp`; `nlohmann/LICENSE.MIT` (MIT).

The receiver independently taps the FM discriminator MPX before stereo filtering, deemphasis, and 48 kHz audio resampling. Its input rate is resampled to 200 kHz, then redsea's unchanged subcarrier chain resamples internally to 171 kHz. RDS is WFM-only with at least 120 kHz channel bandwidth and 128 kHz MPX rate. A narrow channel is not widened automatically.

No upstream runtime samples or file I/O are shipped. A separate host-only test can consume upstream's `test/resources/mpx-testfile-yksi.flac` after converting it to float PCM; the recording is not included in this repository.
